pages.onMs: 267 median over 15 loads (234-718). Three alternating sets gave +85, +79, +129. The shipping build on 9444 gave 182 vs 273 (+91), with 1 of 5 loads at 722.
pages.breakdown: Medians per Sift-on load (n=15, load 0.7-2.9). (1) The title entered the DOM at 163 ms (137-277). (2) The first look that saw it started 11 ms later (8-33). It ran from the MutationObserver callback, because the 16 ms floor applies while parsing with an empty view. In 4 of 15 loads that look found only 'Bread' (see bimodal). The next look was then held by 3x the 58-68 ms title look (150-207 ms) and started at 410-491. (3) The look that showed content took 84 ms (56-282): extraction 66 (48-213), Preact render 3, then 7 ms of work after the render (openAtPost 4-11, AI prep 3-5). The article look in slow loads took 164-266 ms with budget=50 and cut=false. A traced slow load's article look took 138 ms: extraction 92 (walk 49, findArticle 12, findTop 11, findNav 8), render 13, openAtPost 14 (a forced layout from reading scrollTop), processAi 11 (with no API key). (4) Render to frame: 9 ms (1-32). (5) The page's own title frame came at 263 with Sift on vs 182 off (+81). Every look runs inside the parser's task, from the observer, so the page's first frame waits for it. Sift ran 89 ms of JS before that frame (74-119). DOMContentLoaded came 519 ms later with Sift on: article looks of 160-440 ms each ran inside parser tasks while the article streamed in. Fonts, shield and boot cost under 3 ms each.
pages.cause: The usual case is a single 60-85 ms look run inside the parser task right when the title arrives. That look delays both Sift and the page's own first frame by about 80 ms. The slow case is the parser-chunk lottery plus the 3x hold, followed by a full-article look that the 50 ms budget does not bound.

pages.breakdown: (1) The h1 entered the DOM at 158 ms (128-220). (2) The look that saw it started 66 ms later (2-106), almost all of it held by the rule (65). In the trace, findSearch took 22, findNav 14, findArticle 9 and findTop 5.5 before the walk (60). Forced style and layout inside the look took 44 ms. (4) Render to frame: 3 ms. pages.cause: The 16 ms floor turns into a 100 ms floor as soon as parsing ends, and the content look then costs about 140 ms because the budget never cuts it (50 ms of work before the walk, then 256 elements before the first deadline check).

The look runs as a microtask inside YouTube's own long render task, and the frame waits for that task to end. The original's results paint in the same frame. (5) Sift ran 105 ms of JS before the results (85-131): 13-15 looks of 1-14 ms each, plus the observer. Load during this set was 3.1-4.4, driven by YouTube rendering in my own Chrome. Bisect with debug flags, fresh profile, 6 rounds per variant, results-in-DOM medians: off 2268, on 2814, hidden (looks and observer run, view display:none) 2254, nolook (view shows only its boot 'Loading' line) 2198, nolook+nomo 2161, noshield 2679, nofont 2331. Across all 42 bisect loads, whatever the variant: loads whose first contentful paint came before 1000 ms got results at a median of 2727 (n=14). Loads whose first paint came after got 2231 (n=28). With Sift off, the first frame is YouTube's own, at 1130-1530. With Sift on, Sift's first look (the adapter's loading view) paints at 650-1050. In one traced on-load, YouTube rendered its results in a requestIdleCallback from scheduler.js (timeout 3000), requested at 2809, fired at 3174 just after the load event, and ran 1097 ms. The load event itself was later with Sift on in the fresh profile (1520-2246 vs 1466-1604). Sift's view loaded no images before the load event.
pages.cause: It is not Sift's CPU time. The delay follows Sift painting its view before YouTube's own first paint. Hiding the view while all looks still run removes it, and the first-paint split holds across every variant. Inference, not proven: once the document paints, Chrome renders frames during YouTube's startup, and YouTube's idle-callback scheduler gets its idle time later. Font loading and the shield are not shown to matter. The nofont variant also moved first paint, so it is confounded.

commonCauses:
1. Empty looks are not cheap, and their cost then holds the content look back (GitHub repo, issues and file; Wikipedia's slow case). A look that finds nothing still costs 50-100 ms on big pages. Two reasons:
- extractAll runs findSearch, findTop, findNav, mainRoot and findArticle before any walk.
- The first getBoundingClientRect or checkVisibility after the page's CSS arrives pays the page's whole style recalc and layout (24-46 ms in traces).
schedule() then holds the next look until lastRunAt + max(soon ? 16 : 100, 3 x lastDur), in index.ts around line 1641. So the content look starts 60-210 ms after the content is in the DOM. The 3x rule treats a forced recalc the browser would do anyway as Sift's cost.

2. The 16 ms floor holds only while readyState is 'loading' and thinView is true. It drops to 100 ms in two cases:
- The view is a title plus a form or actions (Amazon's sort select and count line; GitHub's repo header).
- Parsing ends between the content arriving and its timer firing (Guardian, +65 ms).
In both cases the 100 ms counts from the last look's start.

3. The 50 ms first-look budget does not bound the look. pastDeadline() is checked only in visitEl, after 256 visible elements and then every 32 (generic.ts line 237). Nothing bounds the work before the walk, or findDialog after it. Adapters ignore the budget. Content looks ran with budget=50 and cut=false at 66-135 ms of extraction (median by page), up to 242 ms. Only GitHub issues ever cut.

4. Work after the render runs in the same task, before the frame (7-22 ms median):
- privatePage, about 12 ms on Amazon. It runs in processAi even with no API key.
- portal layout(), 11-13 ms on Guardian.
- openAtPost reads document.scrollingElement.scrollTop, 8-14 ms on GitHub and Wikipedia.
- fillScreen reads host.scrollHeight, 5-18 ms on BBC and Amazon.
These last three force the layout of the new view. Preact's render itself is 2-7 ms.

5. Looks run inside MutationObserver callbacks, which means inside the HTML parser's task. The page's own first content frame is 45-87 ms later with Sift on (Wikipedia, Guardian, Amazon, BBC). DOMContentLoaded is 170-520 ms later (820 on the GitHub file), because long looks repeat during parsing.

6. The page's own long tasks (GitHub's scripts after parsing) make due timers fire late (median 38-49 ms of the wait). They also hold the frame after Sift's render (GitHub issues, up to 185 ms). On GitHub, navigatesuccess then calls schedule(0), which forces an immediate full look 50-100 ms after the first view.

7. YouTube: Sift's early first paint, not its JS (see the YouTube entry).

Ruled out as first-view causes:
- Font loading. The fetch finishes in a later task; adding a face costs under 2 ms.
- The shield. refreshShield costs 0-1 ms per look, and the noshield variant did not help YouTube.
- Boot and the first render: 1-3 ms.
- Content-script compile and boot: about 20 ms, up to 44 ms under trace. It is the same with Sift on and off.

The debug build agrees with the shipping build on 9444 within 10-45 ms on Wikipedia, GitHub repo, Amazon and BBC. Every main difference here is over 50 ms and repeats in all 3 alternating sets. These smaller or noisier items did not hold across sets:
- Guardian page frame +45: +49, +3, +49.
- GitHub repo page frame: -46, +146, +187.

Load was 0.7-3.1 for all sets except YouTube set a, which ran at 3.1-4.4, mostly from YouTube rendering in my own Chrome. Times are per load, in ms since navigation start.
bimodal:
Wikipedia's bimodality comes from how far the HTML parser had got when Sift's first look ran, plus the probe's 20-character threshold.

- The first look runs right after the parser chunk that contains the h1 (about 1180-1230 nodes). It runs from the MutationObserver, under the 16 ms floor.
- Where that chunk ends varies by network and parser timing. The look found either:
  - only the title, 'Bread', 5 characters (4 of 15 loads);
  - the title plus the 'From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia' tagline;
  - the title plus the infobox;
  - the title plus the start of the article (3 of 5 loads in set b).
- firstpaint.ts needs more than 20 characters, so 'Bread' alone does not count as content.

In the 4 title-only loads:
- thinView keeps the view 'empty'.
- The next look is held by 3x the 58-68 ms title look.
- It then reads the partial article for 164-266 ms with budget=50 and cut=false.
- So the probe sees Sift's content at a median of 670 ms (656-718), against the original's title at about 180.

In the other 11 loads the probe sees content at about 258 ms.

The article body itself is bimodal for the same reason:
- If the first look reached the article, the body showed at 229-262 ms.
- Otherwise it showed with the third look, ending at about 510-680 ms.

The shipping build on 9444 showed the same pattern: 1 of 5 loads at 722 ms, the rest at 263-275. So the bimodality comes from when looks fall relative to parser chunks, the 3x hold after a title-only look, and an article look the budget does not bound. The work per look does not change between the two modes.

Debug build:
- mkdbg.ts <index.ts> <out> writes the debug variant of src/content/index.ts. Every anchor must match once, so it fails loudly if index.ts has changed. index.orig.ts is today's base and index.dbg.ts is the output.
- Its performance.mark names all start with 'DBG ':
  - cs-start (prepended to content.js), boot, boot render start/end, boot end, flags
  - sched <why> now|wait=|kept|overdue|delay= (why: mo, mo-grew, mo-minor, dcl, load, cut, boot, navsuccess, popstate, reread, pagedialog, wake, consent)
  - fire <why> set= d= late=
  - run start #n why= rs= sel= fp= cut= empty= mo= nodes=
  - run extracted <ms> budget= cut= src= partial= blocks= items= kinds=
  - run same
  - paint start, paint end hit=
  - post portals, post shield, post layout, post ai, post fill, post openAtPost, post toEnd
  - run end <ms> hit=
  - mo <ms> (callbacks over 2 ms)
  - font fetch/fetched/loaded/added, dcl, load
- It reads these sessionStorage keys:
  - sift:dbgsel (the original's selector, for sel=)
  - sift:dbgsift (Sift's selector, for hit=)
  - sift:dbgflags, comma list: nolook, nomo, noshield, nofont, nofocus, hidden
- To build it:
  1. cp perf16/index.dbg.ts src/content/index.ts
  2. SIFT_OUT=dist-dbg bun scripts/build.ts
  3. cp perf16/index.orig.ts src/content/index.ts
  4. sha1sum -c perf16/src.sha1
  5. rm dist-dbg/local-key.json
  6. sed -i '1i performance.mark("DBG cs-start");' dist-dbg/content.js
  7. SIFT_OUT=dist-dbg SIFT_PORT=9475 ./scripts/chrome.sh start (or reload)

Measurement scripts (run with SIFT_PORT and SIFT_TAB set):
- loads.ts <url> <sel> <runsPerSide> <out.jsonl> [--sift css] [--block amazon] [--only on|off] [--flags f+g] [--wait ms]: the firstpaint probe, Sift off and on in ABBA order. Per load it adds: when the selector entered the DOM (page-world MutationObserver), every frame time, long tasks, and all DBG marks.
- batch.sh <suffix> <names...>: runs loads.ts with 5 per side for wiki, ghrepo, ghissues, ghfile, guardian, ytsearch, amzsearch and bbc, waiting until load is 3 or less. It logs to batch-<suffix>.log.
- show.ts <jsonl> [on|off|all] [extraMs]: per-load timeline of marks, probe events, long tasks and frame gaps.
- analyze16.ts and breakdown.ts <jsonl...>: per-load and median breakdown. Parts: content in DOM; wait, split into rule hold and page busy, with the look before it; look cost split into extract, render and after-render (shield, portal layout, AI prep, fill, openAtPost); render to frame; page-frame and DOMContentLoaded delay; Sift JS before the page's frame.
- ranges.ts: median and range per page over sets a, b and c.
- wikimodes.ts <wiki jsonl...>: classifies Wikipedia loads by what the first look found.
- ab16.ts <url> <sel> <rounds> <variants> <out.jsonl> [--sift css] [--block amazon]: round-robin bisect of 'off', 'on' and 'on:flag+flag' variants in one tab.
- trace16.ts <url> <sel> <on|off> <name> [--sift css] [--block amazon]: one traced load, after a warm-up load. Env: T, FLAGS, EXTRA_CATS. It writes trace-<name>-<mode>.json.
- tan16.ts <trace> [--until probe-sift|probe-orig|probe-domin|ms] [--fns N] [--look k]: main-thread split per task and per look, with Sift JS, style and layout forced by Sift vs by the page, and the hottest Sift functions in the content look. One fix to note: ProfileChunk events sit on another thread id, so they are matched by Profile id.
- loadres.ts <url> <sel> <n>: resources before the load event, and Sift's view images.
- yta.ts: a YouTube idle-callback and frame summary. It is unreliable, because tracing YouTube slows it too much.
